patch.value: Candidate B1B delivers a Markdown-to-static-site generator using a monolithic CLI pipeline (O1) with a thin-slice milestone strategy. Five milestones incrementally build a fully functional static site: (1) CLI skeleton with Markdown ingestion and single-note HTML rendering, (2) tag extraction and tag pages, (3) internal link resolution and backlinks, (4) client-side search, and (5) polish including broken-link warnings, base-URL configuration, GFM extensions, and cross-browser QA. Each milestone produces a deployable static site with progressively more features, de-risking integration early. The monolithic architecture minimizes design overhead and is intended for a single-user workflow; scale assumptions (e.g., ≤1,000 notes) must be confirmed (Q3) to validate the in-memory approach. Key risks around link conventions (K2) and tag conventions (K3) are front-loaded into Milestones 2–3 with explicit configuration requirements. Scale risks (K4/K5) are deferred pending confirmed target scale. Privacy risk (K8) is accepted with documentation-only mitigation.

Target note scale must be confirmed (Q3). The current design assumes in-memory processing (O1) is sufficient for small-to-medium collections (e.g., ~1,000 notes) and proposes validating search performance against R22 during Milestone 4; if confirmed scale is larger, revisit architecture/mitigations for K4/K5.
